finding.title: profiles_tutoring_p2_test.dart E2E-721 rename sub-test silently no-ops via bare `return` instead of failing when its UI selector isn't found
finding.why: If the ProfilePickerScreen long-press affordance is ever renamed, removed, or regressed so neither 'Edit name' nor 'Rename' text renders, execution hits this early return and the test PASSES without ever reaching lines 519-547 — the actual point of the test ('DuplicateProfileNameException -> snackbar shown; name unchanged in Drift'). No `// weaken-ok:` marker documents this bail-out per the project's own convention for intentional assertion-weakening, so a future reviewer has no signal this branch quietly exists.
finding.recommendation: Fail loudly (`fail('rename affordance not found — check ProfilePickerScreen long-press menu')`) instead of returning silently, or resolve the ambiguity once via a stable Key/tooltip on the rename action so the ambivalent selector isn't needed at all.
acceptance_criteria: The test fails (not silently passes) when neither the 'Edit name' nor 'Rename' affordance is found.
A temporary regression check (rename the button label in source) confirms the test now fails instead of passing green.

finding.title: progress_p1_test.dart E2E-806 claims to verify the documented R-PG7 cross-profile access-control gap but never passes a differing profileId
finding.rule: TQ-8 (assertions weaker than what the source can do wrong / tautological test)

evidence.quote: // profileId here (the tutor sub-test below checks the profileId path

finding.why: The group's own docstring (progress_p1_test.dart:21-22) and R-PG7 registry entry (docs/planning/e2e-test-suite-plan.md:811) both say this journey should 'assert any auth user can load [another profile's data]', but the single test in the group navigates to '/journey' with no profileId query param at all — it loads the caller's own default profile. The comment references 'the tutor sub-test below' that does not exist anywhere in this file. As written the test provides zero signal on R-PG7 in either direction: if the access-control gap is ever fixed, this test won't notice; if it worsens, this test won't notice either.
finding.recommendation: Add the missing sub-test: seed two profiles, request SiyumimMilestonesRoute/journey data for the NON-active profile's id, and assert the returned milestones belong to that other profile — or correct the docstring/comment to stop claiming this scenario is covered here.
acceptance_criteria: A test in this file seeds >=2 profiles and requests journey data via an explicit profileId different from the active profile's.
The assertion checks profile-specific content (not just absence of an error banner) to prove the cross-profile read actually happened.

finding.title: progress_p1_test.dart E2E-812 permanently skipped on a false claim that the harness 'hardcodes Locale(en)' and cannot inject Hebrew

evidence.quote: ///            (harness hardcodes Locale('en'); he locale requires device)
// device/harness: Harness hardcodes Locale("en"); Hebrew-RTL locale

finding.why: E2EHarness.pumpApp takes an overridable `locale` parameter (default only, not hardcoded), and this batch's own overflow_sweep_p2_test.dart already calls it with `locale: const Locale('he')` successfully in headless tests (e.g. lines 499-507, 588-596). The E2E-812 comment's premise is therefore false, and because it asserts the scenario is impossible headlessly, nobody will ever revisit the one-line fix — the whole 'Hebrew locale across all progress screens' journey stays permanently disabled for no real reason.
finding.recommendation: Either implement E2E-812 using the existing `locale: const Locale('he')` parameter (as overflow_sweep_p2_test.dart already does), or delete it as redundant with the equivalent he-locale overflow coverage overflow_sweep_p2_test.dart already provides for ProgressScreen/RecentActivity/LifetimeKnowledge (tests 15/19/20, which default to both locales) and correct the docstring.
acceptance_criteria: The comment no longer claims Locale('he') injection is impossible headlessly.
E2E-812 either runs and passes under Locale('he'), or is removed with a comment pointing at the overlapping overflow-sweep coverage that supersedes it.

finding.title: Assert real toggle/selection state (not just tapped-label presence) in progress_p0_test.dart and scheduler_p0_test.dart chip/segment tests
finding.rule: TQ-7/TQ-8 (assertion weaker than the failure mode under test)

evidence.quote: // The chip label is still visible (toggle rendered without crash).
// Toggle label still visible (no crash, state updated).
// After selecting Dafim, the pace input label should reference "Dafim".

finding.why: Each cited test taps a chip/segment whose label was already visible before the tap (e.g. 'Last 30 Days', 'Track learning only', 'Dafim' are all rendered pre-tap as available options), then re-asserts the SAME label is present post-tap. RecentActivityScreen's chip is a real FilterChip with a `selected` bool the test never reads. A regression that wires onSelected to a no-op — tap does nothing — would leave identical text on screen and pass all 4 tests; one test's own comment even claims 'state updated' while checking only visibility, not state.
finding.recommendation: Assert the actual post-tap state, e.g. `tester.widget<FilterChip>(find.widgetWithText(FilterChip, 'Last 30 Days')).selected == true`, or another concrete tap-dependent effect (chart data range, provider value), instead of re-checking the tapped label's mere presence.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 4 tests asserts a concrete, tap-dependent state change (selected flag, updated derived value, or provider read) rather than only the continued presence of the tapped label.
